concept.name: Payoff ratio
aliases: avg win to avg loss ratio
concept.definition: The ratio of the average winning trade to the average losing trade in a sample, measuring the realized asymmetry between wins and losses. Combined with the win rate it determines expectancy and the breakeven win rate.
concept.intuition: It is the reward per unit of pain a system actually delivers: two systems with equal win rates differ radically if one pays 3R winners and the other 0.5R.
concept.mechanics: Compute the average winner and average loser over the closed-trade sample and divide. It is the realized analogue of the planned risk-reward ratio, which is set before entry; the two diverge whenever exits occur away from the planned stop and target.
concept.formula: Payoff ratio = average winner / average loser; expectancy in units of average losers = p * payoff - (1 - p), with p the win rate.
concept.failure_modes: Outlier wins or losses distort both components, and ratio estimates are noisy on small samples. The realized payoff often differs markedly from the planned reward-to-risk because exits rarely occur exactly at stops and targets.
concept.misconceptions: Payoff ratio and risk-reward ratio are routinely conflated: the former is computed from realized average wins and losses, the latter from intended entry, stop, and target prices.
concept.example: With an average winner of $450 and an average loser of $150, the payoff ratio is 3; the strategy then breaks even at a 25% win rate.
